rolling.label: Rolling Terrain
rolling.description: Gently undulating ground with broad, low rises and shallow hollows.

valleys.label: Valleys
valleys.description: Broad valley floors enclosed by higher ground. The surrounding slopes constrain usable space and routes.

floodplains.label: Floodplains
floodplains.description: Low river plains shaped by flooding and deposited sediment. Water control and soil fertility are separate conditions.

deltas.label: Deltas
deltas.description: Low coastal plains built by river sediment, crossed by distributary channels and exposed to changing water levels.

assumptions: All 22 native topography definitions are retained. New values refine ordinary terrestrial locations; mapped deltas may also refine wetlands. Salt pans, atolls, wastelands, water and non-ownable locations retain their native class.
Global modern geomorphology is an approximation for 1300. Deltas and floodplain courses have greater historical uncertainty; no claim of exact medieval coastlines.

Rolling terrain uses EcoTapestry smooth plains/low hills with 15-180m local relief on ETOPO 1 arc-minute elevation. Valleys use Geomorpho90m valley pixels plus adjacent flat floor within 1km, with at least 80m surrounding relief.

Floodplains use GFPLAIN geomorphic extent supplemented by mapped GLWD riverine settings. GFPLAIN missing background is not proof of no floodplain; small rivers, arid areas and high latitudes have weaker evidence.
Deltas use the convex hull of five published Edmonds et al. points, clipped to ETOPO land below 100m. This is a simplified elevation screen, not an exact reproduction of the authors elevation mask.
Classification priority: deltas, floodplains, valleys, rolling; all source fractions are retained independently. Thresholds are shared global representation rules, not historical measurements.
New values inherit flatland mechanics for this geography prototype. Exact-key vanilla scripts require later integration; no new agricultural balance is asserted.
